newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Credit Suisse Group l-term.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Credit Suisse Group l-term.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Friday it had downgraded its long-term rating of the Credit Suisse Group to AA minus from AA.
It also said it had lowered the long-term ratings of Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) and Credit Suisse Financial Products to AA from AA plus.
IBCA said its long-term rating of Credit Suisse, the domestic bank, was affirmed at AA minus. It added all the entities' short-term ratings of A1 plus were maintained.

"CSFB has established a good presence in many global investment banking markets but faces significant challenges to fully realise the potential of its franchise in an increasingly competitive environment," IBCA said in a statement.
"Similar to many global financial institutions, the group is striving to improve profitability as a result of growing pressure to satisfy shareholder value."

IBCA said its recent restructuring should aid in that effort but added it was also likely CSFB would produce more volatile results, especially in comparison with the former Credit Suisse (Schweizerische Kreditanstalt), which had lower returns but generally a more diversified and stable income stream.

"IBCA's lowering of CSFB's Long-term rating reflects the agency's concerns about the likely increase in its volatility and risk profile as it tries to improve its returns in a more competitive global investment banking market," the rating agency said.
It said its downgrading of CSFP, an unlimited company which is 80%-owned by CSFB, resulted from its dependence on the ratings of its main shareholder.
